title: Nice Grassy Turkish Wagyu Dumplings
description: A hearty Turkish dish featuring tender Wagyu beef dumplings served in a rich and savory grassy broth, perfect for a cozy evening meal. This dish is kosher-friendly and made with fresh ingredients.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine the ground Wagyu beef, chopped onion, minced garlic, chopped parsley, chopped dill, salt, and black pepper, and mix well.
Gradually add the all-purpose flour to the beef mixture and mix until a dough forms.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Divide the dough into small pieces and shape each piece into a dumpling.
Bring the chicken broth to a boil in a large pot and gently add the dumplings.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer the dumplings for 15 minutes or until they float to the surface.
Serve the dumplings hot in the grassy broth, garnished with additional chopped parsley and dill if desired.
Let the dumplings rest for 5 minutes before serving to allow the flavors to meld together.
Traditionally, Turkish dumplings are served with a side of crusty bread or over mashed potatoes.
To add an extra layer of flavor, a dollop of sour cream or a sprinkle of sumac can be added on top.
Leftover dumplings can be refrigerated for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months.
Ensure poultry is cooked to an internal temperature of 74°C / 165°F (juices run clear, no pink remaining) before serving.
